title.zh: 卷六十 唐書36: 列傳12 李襲吉 王緘 李敬義 盧汝弼 李德休 蘇循
title.en: Volume 60 Book of Later Tang 36: Biographies 12 - Li Xiji, Wang Jian, Li Jingyi, Lu Rubi, Li Dexiu, Su Xun
title.raw: 卷六十 唐書36: 列傳12 李襲吉 王緘 李敬義 盧汝弼 李德休 蘇循 Volume 60 Book of Later Tang 36: Biographies 12 - Li Xiji, Wang Jian, Li Jingyi, Lu Rubi, Li Dexiu, Su Xun

sentences.zh: 李襲吉，自言左相林甫之後，父圖，為洛陽令，因家焉。

translations.literal: Li Xiji claimed for himself that he was a descendant of Left Chancellor Li Linfu; his father Tu was magistrate of Luoyang, and the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiji claimed descent from the Left Chancellor Li Linfu. His father Tu served as magistrate of Luoyang, and the family made their home there.

sentences.zh: 襲吉乾符末應進士舉，遇亂，避地河中，依節度使李都，擢為鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: At the end of the Qianfu era Xiji sat for the jinshi examination; he encountered turmoil, fled to Hezhong, relied on Military Commissioner Li Du, and was promoted to salt-and-iron commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Qianfu reign Xiji entered the jinshi examinations, but with rebellion abroad he fled to Hezhong and entered the service of Military Commissioner Li Du, who raised him to salt-and-iron commissioner.

sentences.zh: 及王重榮代，不喜文士，時喪亂之後，衣冠多逃難汾、晉間。

translations.literal: When Wang Chongrong replaced him, he did not favor literary men; after the disorders of the age, gentry in official dress mostly fled for refuge between Fen and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chongrong took his place, the new commissioner had little use for scholars; in the wake of the civil wars, men of the official class fled in droves to the Fen and Jin region.

sentences.zh: 襲吉訪舊至太原，武皇署為府掾，出宰榆社。

translations.literal: Xiji, visiting old acquaintances, came to Taiyuan; the Martial Emperor appointed him a staff officer of the commandery and sent him out as magistrate of Yushe.
translations.idiomatic: Xiji followed old ties to Taiyuan, where the Martial Emperor Li Keyong named him a headquarters aide and later sent him out to govern Yushe county.

sentences.zh: 光啟初，武皇遇難上源，記室歿焉，既歸鎮，辟掌奏者，多不如旨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Guangqi era the Martial Emperor met disaster at Shangyuan and his recorder died there; after he returned to his command, those he recruited to manage memorials mostly failed to please him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangqi reign the Martial Emperor suffered the Shangyuan debacle, and his chief recorder died in the affair. Back in his headquarters he tried one memorialist after another, but few could satisfy him.

sentences.zh: 或有薦襲吉能文，召試稱旨，即署為掌書記。

translations.literal: Someone recommended that Xiji was skilled at writing; he was summoned for a trial and pleased the ruler, and was immediately appointed chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Someone praised Xiji's literary gifts; summoned for a trial draft, he pleased the prince at once and was named chief secretary on the spot.

sentences.zh: 襲吉博學多通，尤諳悉國朝近事，為文精意練實，動據典故，無所放縱，羽檄軍書，辭理宏健。

translations.literal: Xiji was broadly learned and widely versed, especially well acquainted with recent affairs of the dynasty; in writing he refined his meaning and condensed substance, constantly citing precedents without license, and in urgent dispatches and military documents his rhetoric was grand and forceful.
translations.idiomatic: Xiji was erudite and widely read, with a specialist's grasp of recent court history. His prose was tight and concrete, every line anchored in precedent, never florid; whether drafting battle orders or field reports, his style was vigorous and commanding.

sentences.zh: 自武皇上源之難，與梁祖不協，乾寧末，劉仁恭負恩，其間論列是非，交相聘答者數百篇，警策之句，播在人口，文士稱之。

translations.literal: From the Martial Emperor's Shangyuan disaster, through his breach with the Liang Founder and, at the end of Qianning, Liu Rengong's ingratitude, in the exchanges that argued right and wrong back and forth there were several hundred pieces; striking lines spread on people's lips, and literary men praised them.
translations.idiomatic: From the Shangyuan crisis through the rupture with the Liang Founder and, late in Qianning, Liu Rengong's betrayal, Xiji drafted hundreds of letters debating blame and merit between the rival camps. His sharpest lines passed from mouth to mouth, and men of letters spoke of him with admiration.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷節度副使，從討王行瑜，拜右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to deputy military commissioner, followed the campaign against Wang Xingyu, and was appointed Right Remonstrance Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of his service he became deputy military commissioner, marched against Wang Xingyu, and received appointment as Right Remonstrance Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 及師還渭北，武皇不獲入覲，為武皇作違離表，中有警句云：「穴禽有翼，聽舜樂以猶來；

translations.literal: When the army returned to the north of the Wei, the Martial Emperor could not gain an audience; Xiji drafted for him a memorial on being kept apart, containing striking lines that read: "The cave-dwelling bird has wings; hearing Shun's music it would still return;
translations.idiomatic: When the army withdrew north of the Wei, the Martial Emperor was denied an imperial audience. Xiji wrote his master's petition of separation, with lines that ran: "Even a bird that nests in caves will spread its wings; hearing the music of Shun, it would still return;

sentences.zh: 天路無梯，望堯雲而不到。

translations.literal: the road to Heaven has no ladder; gazing at Yao's clouds one cannot arrive."
translations.idiomatic: yet the road to Heaven has no ladder, and though one gazes at the clouds of Yao, one cannot reach them."

sentences.zh: 」昭宗覽之嘉歎。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong read it and sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong read the memorial and sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 洎襲吉入奏，麵詔諭之，優賜特異。

translations.literal: When Xiji came in to present the memorial, the emperor addressed him face to face and bestowed exceptional favors.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiji presented the memorial in person, the emperor received him with a personal audience and lavished extraordinary gifts upon him.

sentences.zh: （《北夢瑣言》：習吉從李克用至渭南，令其入奏，帝重其文章，授諫議大夫，使上事北省以榮之。）〉

translations.literal: (Northern Dreams, Trivial Tales: Xiji followed Li Keyong to Weinan; the prince had him enter court with a memorial. The emperor valued his writings, appointed him Remonstrance Grand Master, and had him report to the northern secretariat to honor him.)]
translations.idiomatic: (Northern Dreams, Trivial Tales: Xiji accompanied Li Keyong to Weinan and was sent to present a memorial at court. The emperor prized his prose, named him Remonstrance Grand Master, and had him report to the northern secretariat as a mark of honor.)]

sentences.zh: 其年十二月，師還太原，王珂為浮梁於夏陽渡，襲吉從軍，時笮斷航破，武皇僅免，襲吉墜河，得大冰承足，沿流七八里，還岸而止，救之獲免。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year the army returned to Taiyuan; Wang Ke built a pontoon bridge at Xiayang Ford and Xiji followed the campaign. At the time the bridge cables broke and the crossing was destroyed; the Martial Emperor barely escaped. Xiji fell into the river, found a great floe of ice to bear his feet, drifted with the current seven or eight li, stopped when he reached the bank, and was rescued and spared.
translations.idiomatic: That December, as the army marched back to Taiyuan, Wang Ke threw a pontoon bridge across the Xiayang ford and Xiji went with the column. The bridge cables snapped mid-crossing; the Martial Emperor barely escaped with his life. Xiji plunged into the river, caught a great slab of ice underfoot, and drifted seven or eight li downstream before he could claw his way ashore and be pulled out alive.

sentences.zh: 天復中，武皇議欲修好於梁，命襲吉為書以貽梁祖，書曰：

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era the Martial Emperor deliberated on restoring good relations with Liang and ordered Xiji to draft a letter to the Liang Founder; the letter read:
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu reign the Martial Emperor resolved to reopen relations with Liang and charged Xiji to draft a letter to the Liang Founder. It read:

sentences.zh: 一別清德，十有餘年，失意杯盤，爭鋒劍戟。

translations.literal: Once we parted in pure virtue, more than ten years have passed; cups and dishes brought disappointment, and swords and spears vied in clash.
translations.idiomatic: Since we parted in mutual regard, more than ten years have passed—shared cups turned to estrangement, and blades crossed in place of toasts.

sentences.zh: 山長水闊，難追二國之歡；

translations.literal: mountains stretch long and waters spread wide, hard to recover the joy of two states;
translations.idiomatic: Mountains lie between us and rivers run wide, so the old warmth of two allied states is hard to recover;

sentences.zh: 雁逝魚沉，久絕八行之賜。

translations.literal: wild geese have flown off and fish sunk deep, and for long the gift of an eight-line letter has been cut off.
translations.idiomatic: the wild goose is gone and the fish lies sunk in the deep—your eight-line letters have long ceased to come.

sentences.zh: 比者仆與公實聯宗姓，原忝恩行，投分深情，將期棲托，論交馬上，薦美朝端，傾向仁賢，未省疏闕。

translations.literal: Of late your servant and you were in truth linked by clan name, and I was unworthy of your gracious conduct; we pledged deep affection and looked to shelter together, made friends on horseback, praised each other at court, and inclined toward the humane and worthy—I never perceived any neglect.
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago we were bound by clan ties and I was unworthy of your kindness; we pledged our hearts to each other and looked to shelter under the same roof, struck up friendship in the saddle, praised each other at court, and leaned toward what was humane and worthy—I never thought you distant.

sentences.zh: 豈謂運由奇特，謗起奸邪。

translations.literal: Who would have said that fate arose from the strange, and slander rose from the wicked?
translations.idiomatic: Who could have foreseen that fate would take so strange a turn, and that slander would rise from the wicked?

sentences.zh: 毒手尊拳，交相於幕夜；

translations.literal: poisonous hands and honored fists were exchanged in the curtain of night;
translations.idiomatic: Poisonous hands and clenched fists met under cover of night;

sentences.zh: 金戈鐵馬，蹂踐於明時。

translations.literal: golden spears and iron horses trampled and trod in the bright age.
translations.idiomatic: golden spears and iron horses trampled the bright age itself.

sentences.zh: 狂藥致其失歡，陳事止於堪笑。

translations.literal: Mad medicine caused the loss of good feeling; the matters set forth ended only in what could be laughed at.
translations.idiomatic: Rash acts born of wine broke our good feeling; the incidents you cite are fit only for laughter.

sentences.zh: 今則皆登貴位，盡及中年，蘧公亦要知非，君子何勞用壯。

translations.literal: Now we have all ascended to exalted rank and all reached middle age; even Duke Qu must know his error—why should a gentleman trouble to use his prime strength?
translations.idiomatic: Now we both stand in high office and have reached middle age; even Duke Qu of old came to know his mistake—why should gentlemen still strain their prime?

sentences.zh: 今公貴先列辟，名過古人。

translations.literal: Now you are honored before the feudal lords of the age, and your fame surpasses the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: You now outrank the feudal lords of the age, and your fame surpasses the ancients.

sentences.zh: 合縱連衡，本務家邦之計；

translations.literal: to ally vertically and join horizontally is fundamentally a plan for one's house and state;
translations.idiomatic: Vertical alliances and horizontal leagues are fundamentally plans for house and state;

sentences.zh: 拓地守境，要存子孫之基。

translations.literal: to expand territory and guard borders is to preserve the foundation for one's sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: to expand territory and hold your borders is to preserve a foundation for your sons and grandsons.

sentences.zh: 文王貴奔走之交，仲尼譚損益之友，仆顧慚虛薄，舊忝眷私，一言許心，萬死不悔，壯懷忠力，猶勝他人，盟於三光，願赴湯火。

translations.literal: King Wen valued friends who ran on his errands; Confucius spoke of friends who could speak of gain and loss. Your servant looks back ashamed at his emptiness and shallowness, yet was once unworthy of your private favor; one word pledged the heart, and ten thousand deaths bring no regret. My stout breast of loyalty and strength still surpasses other men; I swear by sun, moon, and stars and am willing to walk through boiling water and fire.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen prized friends who came running at his call; Confucius spoke of companions who could tell gain from loss. I know myself shallow and unworthy, yet I was once honored with your private regard; one pledged word bound my heart, and I would not repent though I died ten thousand deaths. My loyal strength still outmatches other men; I swear by sun, moon, and stars and would walk through fire and boiling water for you.

sentences.zh: 公又何必終年立敵，懇意相窺，徇一時之襟靈，取四郊之倦弊，今日得其小眾，明日下其危牆，弊師無遺鏃之憂，鄰壤抱剝床之痛。

translations.literal: Why must you stand as enemy year after year, earnestly peering and probing, indulging a moment's temper and drawing on the weariness of the four suburbs—today gaining a small band, tomorrow taking down a perilous wall—so that a ruined army has no worry of leaving arrows behind and neighboring lands embrace the pain of the bed stripped bare?
translations.idiomatic: Why keep an enemy year on year, probing and testing, indulging a passing mood and draining the weary countryside—winning a skirmish today and storming a crumbling wall tomorrow—until broken armies leave arrows on the field and neighboring lands suffer the ruin the Book of Changes calls "the bed stripped bare"?

sentences.zh: 又慮悠悠之黨，妄瀆聽聞，見仆韜勇枕威，戢兵守境，不量本末，誤致窺覦。

translations.literal: I also fear that idle factions will rashly pollute what reaches your ears, seeing your servant hide courage and rest on prestige, sheath arms and guard borders, and, without weighing root and branch, mistakenly provoke covetous glances.
translations.idiomatic: I fear too that loose tongues in your camp will mislead you: seeing me hoard strength and rest on my reputation, sheathe arms and hold my borders, they may mistake restraint for weakness and tempt you to covetous designs.

sentences.zh: 且仆自壯歲已前，業經陷敵，以殺戮為東作，號兼並為永謀。

translations.literal: Moreover, from before my prime your servant has already plunged among enemies, taking slaughter as spring plowing and calling annexation his lasting plan.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, long before my prime I was already plunging among enemies, treating slaughter as spring plowing and calling conquest my lasting design.

sentences.zh: 及其首陟師壇，躬被公兗，天子命我為群後，明公許我以下交，所以斂跡愛人，蓄兵務德，收燕薊則還其故將，入蒲阪而不負前言。

translations.literal: When I first ascended the commander's altar and personally received the ducal regalia, the Son of Heaven ordered me as one of the feudal lords and you, Illustrious Lord, allowed me friendship as with an inferior; therefore I restrained my tracks and cherished men, stored up arms and pursued virtue, and when I took Yan and Ji I returned their former generals, and when I entered Puban I did not betray prior words.
translations.idiomatic: When I first mounted the commander's altar and received the ducal regalia in person, the Son of Heaven named me among the feudal lords and you, Illustrious Lord, treated me as an equal friend; since then I have restrained my conduct and cherished my people, husbanded arms and pursued virtue, restored Yan and Ji's former commanders when I took those lands, and kept my word when I entered Puban.

sentences.zh: 況五載休兵，三邊校士，鐵騎犀甲，雲屯穀量。

translations.literal: Moreover, for five years arms have rested and the three frontiers have drilled soldiers; iron cavalry and rhinoceros-hide armor mass like clouds, and grain is heaped like hills.
translations.idiomatic: For five years my armies have rested while the three frontiers drilled their men; iron cavalry and rhinoceros-hide armor stand massed like clouds, and grain is piled like hills.

sentences.zh: 馬邑兒童，皆為銳將；

translations.literal: the boys of Mayi are all sharp commanders;
translations.idiomatic: The boys of Mayi are all seasoned commanders;

sentences.zh: 鷲峰宮闕，鹹作京坻。

translations.literal: the palaces on Vulture Peak all serve as the capital's granary mound.
translations.idiomatic: the storehouses on Vulture Peak might as well be the capital's granary mound.

sentences.zh: 問年猶少於仁明，語地幸依於險阻，有何覘睹，便誤英聰。

translations.literal: Ask about years and I am still younger than your humane clarity; speak of terrain and I am fortunate to rely on peril and obstruction—what is there to spy out that should mislead your brilliant discernment?
translations.idiomatic: Compare our years and I am still the younger; compare our terrain and I am blessed with natural barriers—what is there for you to reconnoiter that should mislead so keen a mind?

sentences.zh: 況仆臨戎握兵，粗有操斷，屈伸進退，久貯心期。

translations.literal: Moreover, your servant faces battle and holds the army, and has some rough power of decision; bending and stretching, advancing and retreating, he has long stored these in his heart's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I have stood at the head of armies and learned something of command; when to bend, when to strike, when to advance or pull back—these choices I have long weighed in advance.

sentences.zh: 勝則撫三晉之民，敗則征五部之眾，長驅席卷，反首提戈。

translations.literal: If victorious I will soothe the people of the Three Jins; if defeated I will levy the hosts of the Five Divisions; driving far in sweeping advance, I will turn my head and raise spear.
translations.idiomatic: Victory would let me soothe the people of the Three Jins; defeat would still let me rally the Five Divisions; I could drive far and sweep all before me, then wheel about with spear in hand.

sentences.zh: 但慮隳突中原，為公後患，四海群謗，盡歸仁明，終不能見仆一夫，得仆一馬。

translations.literal: I only fear ravaging and striking the Central Plain and making a later trouble for you; the slanders of the four seas would all fall on your humane clarity, and in the end you could not see a single man of mine or obtain a single horse of mine.
translations.idiomatic: I only fear ravaging the Central Plain and leaving you a lasting trouble; the world's blame would fall on your reputation for humanity, and in the end you would not capture a single man or horse of mine.

sentences.zh: 銳師儻失，則難整齊，請防後艱，願存前好。

translations.literal: If sharp troops should be lost, they are hard to set in order again; I beg you to guard against later hardship and wish to preserve our former good feeling.
translations.idiomatic: If elite troops are once broken, they are hard to re-form; guard against later hardship, and let us keep the friendship we once had.

sentences.zh: 矧復陰山部落，是仆懿親；

translations.literal: how much more the tribes of Yin Mountain, who are your servant's close kin;
translations.idiomatic: To say nothing of the Yin Mountain tribes, who are my own close kin;

sentences.zh: 回紇師徒，累從外舍。

translations.literal: the Uighur masters and disciples have repeatedly followed my outer household.
translations.idiomatic: the Uighur hosts have marched beside my house again and again.

sentences.zh: 文靖求始畢之眾，元海征五部之師，寬言虛詞，猶或得志。

translations.literal: Wen Jing sought the hosts of Shibi and Bibi; Yuan Hai levied the armies of the Five Divisions—with broad words and empty phrases they still sometimes achieved their aim.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Jing raised the Shibi and Bibi tribes; Yuan Hai marched the Five Divisions—with empty boasts they still sometimes won their way.

sentences.zh: 今仆散積財而募勇輩，輦寶貨以誘義戎，征其密親，啗以美利，控弦跨馬，寧有數乎！

translations.literal: Now your servant disperses accumulated wealth to recruit bold fellows, carts treasure to entice the righteous barbarians, summons their close kin, feeds them with fine profit—bow in hand, astride horse, can there be any counting them!
translations.idiomatic: Today I scatter my hoarded wealth to recruit warriors, cart treasure to entice the frontier tribes, call up their close kin, and feed them rich reward—who can count the bowmen and horsemen I could field!

sentences.zh: 但緣荷位天朝，惻心疲瘵，峨峨亭障，未忍起戎。

translations.literal: Only because I bear office under the heavenly court, my heart aches for the weary and afflicted, and the towering frontier posts—I cannot bear to raise arms.
translations.idiomatic: Only because I hold office under the Son of Heaven, my heart aches for a worn and afflicted people, and I cannot bear to raise arms along those towering frontier walls.

sentences.zh: 亦望公深識鄙懷，洞回英鑒，論交釋憾，慮禍革心，不聽浮譚，以傷霸業。

translations.literal: I also hope you will deeply know my humble heart, turn your brilliant mirror, discuss friendship and release resentment, consider disaster and change your mind, and not heed floating talk to harm your hegemonic enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: I hope you will read my humble intent aright, turn your keen judgment, renew friendship and lay resentment aside, foresee disaster and change your course, and refuse idle talk that would wound your hegemony.

sentences.zh: 夫《易》惟忌滿，道貴持盈，儻恃勇以喪師，如擎盤而失水，為蛇刻鶴，幸賜徊翔，

translations.literal: The Changes warns only against fullness; the Way esteems holding fullness. If one relies on courage and loses the army, it is like carrying a tray and losing the water, or carving a crane on a snake—I beg you grant me circling flight,
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes warns against excess; the Way values holding one's gains. To lean on courage and lose an army is to carry a full tray and spill the water, or to carve legs on a snake—I beg you grant me room to turn aside,

sentences.zh: 仆少負褊心，天與直氣，間謀詭論，誓不為之。

translations.literal: your servant from youth has borne a narrow heart and Heaven gave him upright spirit; secret plots and crafty arguments he swears never to make.
translations.idiomatic: I have been narrow-spirited since youth, yet Heaven gave me an upright temper; intrigue and crafty argument I swear never to practice.

sentences.zh: 唯將藥石之譚，願托金蘭之分。

translations.literal: I will only offer talk harsh as medicine and stone, and wish to entrust myself to the bond of metal and orchid.
translations.idiomatic: I offer only words harsh as medicine, and ask to renew the bond we once called kin.

sentences.zh: 儻愚衷未豁，彼抱猶迷，假令罄三朝之威，窮九流之辯，遣回肝膈，如俟河清。

translations.literal: If my foolish heart is not opened and your breast still deluded, even if one exhausted the prestige of three courts and exhausted the arguments of the nine schools, to send back the liver and diaphragm would be like waiting for the river to clear.
translations.idiomatic: If my foolish heart cannot reach you and your mind stays closed, then even exhausting the prestige of three dynasties and every argument the nine schools know would not open your breast—it would be like waiting for the Yellow River to run clear.

sentences.zh: 今者執簡吐誠，願垂保鑒。

translations.literal: Now, holding the bamboo slip, I speak my sincerity and beg you to bestow your safeguarding mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Now, brush in hand, I speak plainly and beg your careful regard.

sentences.zh: 仆自眷私睽隔，翰墨往來，或有鄙詞，稍侵英聽，亦承嘉論，每賜罵言。

translations.literal: Since private favor was divided, brush and ink have gone back and forth; sometimes coarse words have slightly offended your brilliant hearing, yet I have also received fine discourse and been repeatedly granted words of scolding.
translations.idiomatic: Since our private bond was broken, letters have flown back and forth; some of my words may have been coarse and grated on your ear, yet I have also received your fine replies—and your scolding, which I took as kindness.

sentences.zh: 敘歡既罷於尋戈，焚謗幸蠲其載筆，窮因尚口，樂貴和心，願祛沉閼之嫌，以復塤篪之好。

translations.literal: Joy in reunion has already ended in seeking spears; burning slander fortunately cancels what the brush recorded. In extremity one still esteems the mouth; in pleasure one values harmony of heart. I wish to remove the suspicion of deep blockage and restore the good accord of xun and chi.
translations.idiomatic: Shared joy gave way to drawn swords; let us burn the slanders and erase what the brush recorded. In hardship men still prize honest speech; in friendship they value harmony of heart. Remove the buried grudge between us and restore the old music of pipe and flute.

sentences.zh: 今者卜於嚬分，不欲因人，專遣使乎，直詣鈴閣。

translations.literal: Now, divining on the lines of a frown, I do not wish to rely on another person; I specially send an envoy to go straight to your bell pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the lines of discord in our faces, I will not send another man's words; I dispatch an envoy of my own straight to your command pavilion.

sentences.zh: 古者兵交兩地，使在其間，致命受辭，幸存前誌。

translations.literal: In antiquity when arms clashed between two regions, envoys stood between them, risking life to receive words—fortunately the former records survive.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when two armies met, envoys passed between them at the risk of their lives; fortunately the old chronicles still preserve that precedent.

sentences.zh: 昔賢貴於投分，義士難於屈讎，若非仰戀恩私，安可輕露肝膈，淒淒丹愫，炳炳血情，臨紙向風，千萬難述。

translations.literal: Former worthies prized pledging their portion; men of honor find it hard to bow to enmity. If not for looking up in longing for private favor, how could one lightly expose liver and diaphragm? My crimson heart is desolate, my bloody feeling bright; facing the paper toward the wind, a thousand myriad things are hard to tell.
translations.idiomatic: Worthies of old prized sworn fellowship; men of honor hate to bow to a feud. Had I not still yearned for your private kindness, how could I lay bare my inmost heart? My loyal breast is desolate, my feeling bright as blood; facing this page into the wind, words fail a thousand times over.

sentences.zh: 梁祖覽之，至「毒手尊拳」之句，怡然謂敬翔曰：「李公鬥絕一隅，安得此文士！

translations.literal: The Liang Founder read it, and when he came to the line "poisonous hands and honored fists," he said with pleasure to Jing Xiang: "Lord Li holds a corner of the realm in struggle—how does he obtain such a literary man!
translations.idiomatic: The Liang Founder read the letter, and at the line "poisonous hands and honored fists" he said with pleasure to Jing Xiang, "Lord Li holds only a corner of the empire—where did he find a writer like this!

sentences.zh: 如吾之智算，得襲吉之筆才，虎傅翼矣！

translations.literal: If my schemes had Xiji's brush talent, it would be a tiger given wings!"
translations.idiomatic: If a mind like mine had Xiji's pen, it would be a tiger given wings!"

sentences.zh: 」又讀至「馬邑兒童」、「陰山部落」之句，梁祖怒謂敬翔曰：「李太原殘喘餘息，猶氣吞宇宙，可詬罵之。

translations.literal: Reading further to the lines "boys of Mayi" and "Yin Mountain tribes," the Liang Founder said angrily to Jing Xiang: "Li of Taiyuan is a dying breath with remnants of life, yet still swallows the universe in his spirit—he can be reviled and scolded."
translations.idiomatic: But when he reached "boys of Mayi" and "Yin Mountain tribes," the Founder turned angry and told Jing Xiang, "Li of Taiyuan is a man on his last breath, yet he still talks as if he could swallow the universe—answer him with abuse."

sentences.zh: 」及翔為報書，詞理非勝，由是襲吉之名愈重。

translations.literal: When Jing Xiang drafted the reply, its rhetoric and reasoning did not prevail; because of this Xiji's name grew still heavier.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Xiang drafted the reply, but his prose could not match Xiji's; Xiji's reputation rose all the higher.

sentences.zh: （《通鑒考異》引《唐末見聞錄》載全忠回書云：前年洹水，曾獲賢郎；

translations.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian, Examination of Variants cites Late Tang Eyewitness Records on Quanzhong's reply: "The year before last at Huan River we once captured your worthy son;
translations.idiomatic: (Zizhi Tongjian, Examination of Variants cites Late Tang Eyewitness Records: in his reply Quanzhong wrote, "The year before last at the Huan River we captured your worthy son;

sentences.zh: 去歲青山，又擒列將。

translations.literal: last year at Green Mountain we again took your ranked generals."
translations.idiomatic: last year at Green Mountain we took your commanders again."—

sentences.zh: 蓋梁之書檄，皆此類也。）〉

translations.literal: In general Liang's letters and proclamations were all of this sort.)]
translations.idiomatic: such was the tone of Liang's letters and proclamations.)]

sentences.zh: 自廣明大亂之後，諸侯割據方面，競延名士，以掌書檄。

translations.literal: From after the great disorder of the Guangming era, feudal lords held regions by force and vied to summon famous scholars to manage letters and proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: After the great disorders of the Guangming reign, regional lords carved up the empire and competed to recruit famous scholars to draft their letters and battle proclamations.

sentences.zh: 是時梁有敬翔，燕有馬鬱，華州有李巨川，荊南有鄭準，

translations.literal: At that time Liang had Jing Xiang, Yan had Ma Yu, Hua Prefecture had Li Juchuan, and Jingnan had Zheng Zhun,
translations.idiomatic: Liang had Jing Xiang, Yan had Ma Yu, Hua had Li Juchuan, and Jingnan had Zheng Zhun,

sentences.zh: （《唐新纂》云：鄭準，士族，未第時，佐荊門上穀蓮幕，飛書走檄，不讓古人，秉直去邪，無慚往哲，考準為成汭書記，汭封上穀郡王。）〉

translations.literal: (New Tang Compendium says: Zheng Zhun, of the gentry class, before passing the examinations assisted Shanggu Lian's Jingmen staff office; in flying letters and running proclamations he yielded to no ancients, upheld rectitude and expelled evil without shame before former sages. Examined: Zhun was secretary to Cheng Rui, and Rui was enfeoffed as Prince of Shanggu Commandery.)]
translations.idiomatic: (New Tang Compendium: Zheng Zhun came from the gentry; before he passed the examinations he served on Shanggu Lian's staff at Jingmen, drafting dispatches that matched the ancients and upholding rectitude without shame before the sages of old. He served as secretary to Cheng Rui, who was enfeoffed as Prince of Shanggu.)]

sentences.zh: 鳳翔有王超，

translations.literal: Fengxiang had Wang Chao,
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang had Wang Chao,

sentences.zh: （《北夢瑣言》：唐末，鳳翔判官王超，推奉李茂貞，挾曹、馬之勢，箋奏文檄，恣意翱翔。

translations.literal: (Northern Dreams, Trivial Tales: At the end of Tang, Fengxiang administrative aide Wang Chao promoted and supported Li Maozhen, wielding the power of Cao and Ma; in memorials and military documents he soared as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: (Northern Dreams, Trivial Tales: Late in Tang, Fengxiang aide Wang Chao backed Li Maozhen and wielded power like Cao Cao and Sima Yi; his memorials and battle letters ranged freely wherever he chose.

sentences.zh: 後為興元留後，遇害，有《鳳鳴集》三十卷行於世。）〉

translations.literal: Later he became acting commissioner of Xingyuan and met with violent death; his Phoenix Cry Collection in thirty juan circulated in the world.)]
translations.idiomatic: He later became acting commissioner of Xingyuan, was killed in the turmoil, and left the Phoenix Cry Collection in thirty juan.)]

sentences.zh: 錢塘有羅隱，魏博有李山甫，皆有文稱，與襲吉齊名於時。

translations.literal: Qiantang had Luo Yin, Weibo had Li Shanfu—all had literary fame and were ranked with Xiji in their day.
translations.idiomatic: Qiantang had Luo Yin and Weibo had Li Shanfu; all were famed for their writing and ranked with Xiji in that age.

sentences.zh: 襲吉在武皇幕府垂十五年，視事之暇，唯讀書業文，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: Xiji was in the Martial Emperor's staff office for nearly fifteen years; in the leisure of handling affairs he only read books and pursued writing, his hand never leaving the scroll.
translations.idiomatic: Xiji served in the Martial Emperor's headquarters for nearly fifteen years; in whatever leisure his duties allowed he read and wrote without setting a book down.

sentences.zh: 性恬於榮利，獎誘後進，不以己能格物。

translations.literal: By nature he was indifferent to glory and profit, encouraged and guided juniors, and did not use his own ability to obstruct others.
translations.idiomatic: He cared little for rank or gain, encouraged younger men, and never used his own talent to block others.

sentences.zh: 參決府事，務在公平，不交賂遺，綽綽有士大夫之風概焉。

translations.literal: In deliberating commandery affairs he strove for fairness, accepted no bribes or gifts, and had ample bearing of a scholar-official.
translations.idiomatic: In council he strove for fairness, took no bribes, and bore himself with the ample dignity of a scholar-official.

sentences.zh: 天祐三年六月，以風病卒於太原。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Tianyou he died of wind illness at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Tianyou year three he died of a stroke at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 同光二年，追贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongguang he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongguang year two he was posthumously honored as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 王緘，幽州劉仁恭故吏也。

translations.literal: Wang Jian was a former clerk of Liu Rengong of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian had been a clerk in the service of Liu Rengong of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 少以刀筆直記室，仁恭假以幕職，令使鳳翔。

translations.literal: In youth he served as recorder with brush and knife; Rengong lent him a staff post and sent him as envoy to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he served as recorder in Rengong's secretariat; the lord gave him a staff post and sent him on a mission to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 還經太原，屬仁恭阻命，武皇留之。

translations.literal: Returning he passed through Taiyuan; it happened that Rengong blocked his orders, and the Martial Emperor detained him.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he passed through Taiyuan; Rengong had meanwhile defied the court, and the Martial Emperor detained him.

sentences.zh: 緘堅辭復命，書詞稍抗，武皇怒，下獄詰之，謝罪聽命，乃署為推官，曆掌書記。

translations.literal: Jian firmly declined to return to his commission; his letter's wording was somewhat defiant. The Martial Emperor was angry, put him in prison and interrogated him; he apologized and obeyed orders, and was then appointed investigating officer and successively served as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Jian insisted on returning to complete his mission; his letter was defiant in tone. The Martial Emperor in anger threw him into prison and questioned him. Jian apologized and submitted; he was named investigating officer and later chief secretary.

sentences.zh: （《契丹國誌·韓延徽傳》：延徽自契丹奔晉，晉王欲置之幕府掌書記，王緘嫉之，延徽不自安，求東歸省母，遂復入契丹，寓書於晉王，敘所以北去之意。

translations.literal: (Khitan State Records, Biography of Han Yanhui: Yanhui fled from Khitan to Jin; the Prince of Jin wished to place him in the staff office as chief secretary. Wang Jian envied him; Yanhui was ill at ease, asked to go east to visit his mother, and thus re-entered Khitan. He sent a letter to the Prince of Jin explaining why he went north.
translations.idiomatic: (Khitan State Records, Biography of Han Yanhui: Yanhui fled the Khitan for Jin; the Prince of Jin wished to make him chief secretary. Wang Jian resented him; uneasy in Taiyuan, Yanhui asked leave to visit his mother in the east, returned to the Khitan, and wrote the prince explaining why he had gone north.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「非不戀英主，非不思故鄉，所以不留，正懼王緘之讒耳。」）〉

translations.literal: He also said: "It is not that I do not cherish an enlightened lord, nor that I do not think of my homeland; the reason I do not stay is precisely that I fear Wang Jian's slander.")]
translations.idiomatic: He wrote, "It is not that I do not love an enlightened master or long for home; I dare not stay because I fear Wang Jian's slander.")]

sentences.zh: 從莊宗經略山東，承製授檢校司空、魏博節度使。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Zhuangzong in pacifying Shandong, he received by imperial order appointment as Acting Minister of Works and military commissioner of Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Zhuangzong in the pacification of Shandong and received by imperial order the acting title Minister of Works and the post of military commissioner of Weibo.

sentences.zh: 緘博學善屬文，燕薊多文士，緘後生，未知名，及在太原，名位驟達。

translations.literal: Jian was broadly learned and skilled at composing text; Yan and Ji had many literary men. Jian was younger and not yet known by name; once he was at Taiyuan, fame and rank rose swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was erudite and a fine writer; Yan and Ji had many men of letters, and Jian as a younger man was still unknown—at Taiyuan his name and rank rose overnight.

sentences.zh: 燕人馬鬱，有盛名於鄉里，而緘素以吏職事鬱。

translations.literal: Ma Yu of Yan had great fame in his home district, while Jian had long served Yu in a clerk's post.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yu of Yan enjoyed great local fame, though Jian had long served him in a clerk's capacity.

sentences.zh: 及鬱在太原，謂緘曰：「公在此作文士，所謂避風之鳥，受賜於魯人也。

translations.literal: When Yu was at Taiyuan he said to Jian: "You serve here as a literary man—the so-called bird that flees the wind and receives favor from the man of Lu."
translations.idiomatic: When Yu came to Taiyuan he told Jian, "You play the literary man here—the bird that flees the storm and finds shelter with a stranger in Lu."

sentences.zh: 」每於公宴，但呼王緘而已。

translations.literal: At every public banquet he would only call out "Wang Jian" and nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: At every public feast he would call only "Wang Jian" and use no other name for him.

sentences.zh: 十年，從征幽州，既獲仁恭父子，莊宗命緘為露布，觀其旨趣。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he followed the campaign against Youzhou; after Rengong father and son were captured, Emperor Zhuangzong ordered Jian to draft the victory bulletin to observe his intent.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he marched on Youzhou; after Rengong and his sons were taken, Emperor Zhuangzong ordered Jian to draft the victory bulletin to see where his loyalties lay.

sentences.zh: 緘起草無所辭避，義士以此少之。

translations.literal: Jian drafted it without any evasion or refusal; men of honor therefore thought somewhat less of him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian wrote the bulletin without hesitation or evasion, and men of honor thought less of him for it.

sentences.zh: 胡柳之役，緘隨輜重前行，歿於亂兵。

translations.literal: In the battle at Huliu, Jian followed the baggage train forward and perished among the disorderly troops.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Huliu, Jian marched with the baggage train ahead of the column and was killed in the rout.

sentences.zh: 際晚，盧質還營，莊宗問副使所在，曰：「某醉不之知也。

translations.literal: Near evening Lu Zhi returned to camp; Emperor Zhuangzong asked where the deputy commissioner was, and he said: "I was drunk and do not know."
translations.idiomatic: Near evening Lu Zhi returned to camp; the emperor asked where the deputy commissioner was, and Lu said, "I was drunk and do not know."

sentences.zh: 」既而緘凶問至，莊宗流涕久之，得其喪，歸葬太原。

translations.literal: Soon word of Jian's death arrived; Emperor Zhuangzong wept for a long time, recovered his coffin, and returned it for burial at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Word of Jian's death soon arrived; Emperor Zhuangzong wept a long while, recovered the body, and had it buried at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 李敬義，本名延古，太尉衛公德裕之孫。

translations.literal: Li Jingyi, original name Yangu, was grandson of Grand Preceptor Wei Gong Li Deyu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jingyi, born Yangu, was a grandson of Grand Preceptor Li Deyu of Wei.

sentences.zh: 初隨父煒貶連州，遇赦得還。

translations.literal: At first he followed his father Wei into exile at Lian Prefecture and, meeting an amnesty, was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: He first followed his father Wei into exile at Lianzhou and returned only when an amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 嘗從事浙東，自言遇涿道士，謂之曰：「子方厄運，不宜仕進。

translations.literal: He once served in Zhedong and said himself that he met a Daoist priest of Zhuo, who told him: "You are in a season of ill fortune and should not seek advancement in office."
translations.idiomatic: He once served in eastern Zhe and said he met a Daoist of Zhuo who told him, "You are in an unlucky season and should not pursue office."

sentences.zh: 」敬義悚然對曰：「吾終老賤哉？

translations.literal: Jingyi answered in alarm: "Am I to grow old in low estate?"
translations.idiomatic: Jingyi answered with a start, "Am I then to grow old in obscurity?"

sentences.zh: 」涿曰：「自此四十三年，必遇聖王大任，子其志之。

translations.literal: Zhuo said: "From now, in forty-three years, you will surely meet a sage king's great commission—keep this in mind."
translations.idiomatic: The priest of Zhuo said, "Forty-three years from now you will surely meet a sage king's great commission—remember it."

sentences.zh: 」敬義以為然，乃無心仕宦，退歸洛南平泉舊業。

translations.literal: Jingyi took this as correct, and thus had no heart for office; he withdrew to the old family estate at Pingquan south of the Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyi believed him, lost all appetite for office, and retired to the family's old estate at Pingquan south of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 為河南尹張全義所和，歲時給遺特厚，出入其門，欲署幕職，堅辭不就。

translations.literal: He was befriended by Zhang Quanyi, prefect of Henan; seasonal gifts were especially generous, and he went in and out of his gate. Quanyi wished to appoint him to a staff post, but he firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Henan prefect Zhang Quanyi befriended him and sent lavish seasonal gifts; Jingyi frequented his house, but when Quanyi offered a staff post he firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 初，德裕之為將相也，大有勳於王室，出藩入輔，綿曆累朝；

translations.literal: At first, when Deyu served as general and minister, he had great merit for the royal house, going out to the regions and entering as aide, spanning many reigns;
translations.idiomatic: In his prime, when Deyu served as general and minister, he won great merit for the throne, moving between the provinces and the capital through many reigns;

sentences.zh: 及留守洛陽，有終焉之志，於平泉置別墅，采天下奇花異竹、珍木怪石，為園池之玩。

translations.literal: when he remained to guard Luoyang he had the will to end his days there, established a villa at Pingquan, gathered rare flowers and strange bamboos, precious trees and curious stones from all under Heaven for the pleasure of gardens and ponds.
translations.idiomatic: when he stayed on as guardian of Luoyang he meant to end his days there, built a villa at Pingquan, and gathered rare flowers, exotic bamboos, precious trees, and curious stones from across the empire for his gardens and ponds.

sentences.zh: 自為家戒序錄，誌其草木之得處，刊於石，云：「移吾片石，折樹一枝，非子孫也。

translations.literal: He himself made a family admonition with preface and record, noting where each plant was obtained, carved it on stone, and said: "Whoever moves a single stone of mine or breaks a branch of my trees is not my descendant."
translations.idiomatic: He drew up a family admonition listing where each plant came from and had it carved in stone: "Whoever moves one stone of mine or breaks one branch of my trees is not my descendant."

sentences.zh: 」洎巢、蔡之亂，洛都灰燼，全義披榛而創都邑，李氏花木，多為都下移掘，樵人鬻賣，園亭掃地矣。

translations.literal: By the time of the disorders of Huang Chao and Cai, the Luo capital was ashes; Quanyi cut through brambles to rebuild the city. The Li family's flowers and trees were mostly dug up and transplanted by people of the capital, sold by woodcutters—the gardens and pavilions were swept clean.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellions of Huang Chao and Cai Jing engulfed Luoyang, the capital lay in ashes; Quanyi hacked through the ruins to rebuild the city. The Li family's plants were dug up and carted away, sold by woodcutters until the gardens stood bare.

sentences.zh: 有醒酒石，德裕醉即踞之，最保惜者。

translations.literal: There was a sobering stone; when Deyu was drunk he would sit upon it—the thing he most treasured.
translations.idiomatic: Among them was a sobering stone on which Deyu would sit when drunk—the treasure he guarded most closely.

sentences.zh: 光化初，中使有監全義軍得此石，置於家園。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guanghua, an inner envoy supervising Quanyi's army obtained this stone and placed it in his private garden.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guanghua reign an imperial eunuch supervising Quanyi's army took the stone for his private garden.

sentences.zh: 敬義知之，泣渭全義曰：「平泉別業，吾祖戒約甚嚴，子孫不肖，動違先旨。

translations.literal: Jingyi learned of it and, weeping, told Quanyi at the Wei: "The Pingquan villa—my grandfather's admonitions were very strict; unworthy descendants constantly violate his intent."
translations.idiomatic: When Jingyi learned of it he wept and told Quanyi at the Wei River, "At the Pingquan villa my grandfather's admonitions were strict; his unworthy descendants have again broken his will."

sentences.zh: 」因托全義請石於監軍。

translations.literal: He therefore entrusted Quanyi to request the stone from the supervising commander.
translations.idiomatic: He asked Quanyi to request the stone back from the eunuch commander.

sentences.zh: 他日宴會，全義謂監軍曰：「李員外泣告，言內侍得衛公醒酒石，其祖戒堪哀，內侍能回遺否？

translations.literal: On another day at a banquet Quanyi said to the supervising commander: "Vice Director Li wept and reported that the inner attendant obtained Duke Wei's sobering stone; his grandfather's admonition is pitiable—can the inner attendant return it?"
translations.idiomatic: At a later banquet Quanyi told the eunuch, "Vice Director Li came weeping to say you took Duke Wei's sobering stone; his grandfather's admonition makes the loss pitiable—can you return it?"

sentences.zh: 」監軍忿然厲聲曰：「黃巢敗後，誰家園池完復，豈獨平泉有石哉！

translations.literal: The supervising commander said angrily in a harsh voice: "After Huang Chao's defeat, whose gardens and ponds remained intact—is Pingquan alone in having stones!"
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch snapped back in anger, "After Huang Chao's defeat, whose gardens survived intact? Does Pingquan alone have stones!"

sentences.zh: 」全義始受黃巢偽命，以為詬己，大怒曰：「吾今為唐臣，非巢賊也。

translations.literal: Quanyi had once accepted Huang Chao's false commission and took this as a reproach against himself; he said in great anger: "I am now a minister of Tang, not a bandit of Chao."
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi had once accepted a post under Huang Chao and took the remark as a personal insult; he roared, "I am a minister of Tang now, not Huang Chao's creature."

sentences.zh: 」即署奏笞斃之。

translations.literal: He immediately drafted a memorial to have him beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: He at once drafted a memorial ordering the man flogged to death.

sentences.zh: 昭宗遷都洛陽，以敬義為司勳員外郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong moved the capital to Luoyang, he appointed Jingyi Vice Director in the Bureau of Merits.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong moved the capital to Luoyang, he named Jingyi Vice Director in the Bureau of Merits.

sentences.zh: 柳璨之陷裴、趙諸族，希梁祖旨奏云：「近年浮薄相扇，趨競成風，乃有臥邀軒冕，視王爵如土梗者。

translations.literal: When Liu Can trapped the Pei and Zhao clans, flattering the Liang Founder's intent he memorialized: "In recent years the frivolous have fanned one another and rushing for gain has become the fashion; there are even those who lie in wait for high rank and regard royal titles like clods of earth."
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Can destroyed the Pei and Zhao clans, he flattered the Liang Founder with a memorial: "In recent years the frivolous egg one another on and office-seeking has become a fashion; some even lie in wait for high rank and treat royal titles like dirt."

sentences.zh: 司空圖、李敬義三度除官，養望不至，咸宜屏黜，以勸事君者。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Tu and Li Jingyi have been appointed three times yet nursed their reputation and did not come—all should be removed from office to encourage those who serve their lord.
translations.idiomatic: Sikong Tu and Li Jingyi have been appointed three times yet nursed their reputations and never reported—all should be dismissed to encourage loyal service.

sentences.zh: 」翌日，詔曰：「司勳史外郎李延古，世荷國恩，兩葉相位，幸從筮仕，累忝寵榮，多曆歲時，不趨班列。

translations.literal: The next day an edict said: "Vice Director in the Bureau of Merits Li Yangu, his family having received national favor for generations and two generations as chief ministers, was fortunate to enter office by divination and repeatedly received favor and glory; for many years he has not hastened to court ranks."
translations.idiomatic: The next day an edict ran: "Vice Director Li Yangu's family has borne the state's favor for generations; two generations served as chief ministers. He entered office by fortune and received repeated honors, yet for years he has not attended court ranks."

sentences.zh: 而自遷都卜洛，紀律載張，去明庭而非遙，處別墅而無懼，岡思報效，姑務便安。

translations.literal: Yet since the move of the capital to Luoyang, discipline has been displayed; the bright court is not far, yet dwelling in a villa he shows no fear, hardly thinks of repaying service, and for the moment seeks only ease.
translations.idiomatic: Since the capital moved to Luoyang and discipline was proclaimed, the bright court is not far—yet he dwells in his villa without fear, scarcely thinks of service, and seeks only his own ease.

sentences.zh: 為臣之節如斯，貽厥之謀何在！

translations.literal: The integrity of a minister is like this—where is the plan he leaves to his heirs!
translations.idiomatic: Such is his conduct as a minister—where is the legacy he leaves his heirs!

sentences.zh: 須加懲責，以肅朝倫，九寺勾稽，尚謂寬典，可責授衛尉寺主簿。

translations.literal: Punishment must be added to rectify court order; the Nine Offices' review still calls this a lenient statute—he may be demoted and appointed Recorder of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He must be punished to restore court order; even the Nine Offices' review calls this lenient—demote him to recorder of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 」司空圖亦追停前詔，任從閑適。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Tu also had his prior edict revoked and was allowed to follow leisure as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Sikong Tu's prior appointment was also revoked, and he was left to his leisure.

sentences.zh: 圖，唐史有傳。

translations.literal: Tu has a biography in the Tang histories.
translations.idiomatic: Tu has a biography in the Tang histories.

sentences.zh: （《舊唐書·哀帝紀》：六月戊申，敕前司勳員外郎、賜緋魚袋李延古責授衛尉寺主簿。

translations.literal: (Old Book of Tang, Annals of Emperor Ai: On the wushen day of the sixth month, an edict demoted former Vice Director in the Bureau of Merits, bearer of the crimson fish tally Li Yangu, and appointed him Recorder of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: (Old Book of Tang, Annals of Emperor Ai: On the wushen day of the sixth month, an edict demoted former Vice Director Li Yangu, bearer of the crimson fish tally, to recorder of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 九月壬寅，敕前大中大夫、尚書兵部侍郎、賜紫金魚袋司空圖放還中條山。

translations.literal: On the renyin day of the ninth month, an edict released former Grand Master of Palace Attendance, Vice Minister of War in the Secretariat, bearer of the purple-gold fish tally Sikong Tu to return to Mount Zhongtiao.
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin day of the ninth month, an edict released former Vice Minister of War Sikong Tu, bearer of the purple-gold fish tally, to return to Mount Zhongtiao.

sentences.zh: 蓋延古與司空圖同時被劾，其降敕則有先後也。）〉

translations.literal: In general Yangu and Sikong Tu were impeached at the same time, but the edicts of demotion came in sequence.)]
translations.idiomatic: Yangu and Sikong Tu were impeached together, though the demotion edicts came in sequence.)]

sentences.zh: 時全義既不能庇護，乃密托楊師厚，令敬義潛往依之，因挈族客居衛州者累年，師厚給遺周厚。

translations.literal: At the time Quanyi could no longer protect him and secretly entrusted Yang Shihou to have Jingyi go secretly to rely on him; he thus brought his clan to lodge as guests at Weizhou for many years, and Shihou's gifts were ample and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi could no longer protect him and secretly asked Yang Shihou to take him in; Jingyi brought his clan to live as guests at Weizhou for years, and Shihou supported them generously.

sentences.zh: 十二年，莊宗定河朔，史建瑭收新鄉，敬義謁見。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Emperor Zhuangzong pacified Hebei; Shi Jiantang took Xinxing, and Jingyi paid a visit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Zhuangzong pacified Hebei; when Shi Jiantang took Xinxing, Jingyi came to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 是歲，上遣使迎至魏州，置北京留守判官承製拜工部尚書，奉使王鎔。

translations.literal: That year the emperor sent envoys to welcome him to Weizhou, appointed him acting northern capital guardian investigating officer with imperial commission, and enfeoffed him Minister of Works, sending him as envoy to Wang Rong.
translations.idiomatic: That year the emperor sent envoys to bring him to Weizhou, named him investigating officer of the northern capital with imperial commission, appointed him Minister of Works, and sent him as envoy to Wang Rong.

sentences.zh: 敬義以遠祖趙郡，見鎔展維桑之敬，鎔遣判官李翥送《讚皇集》三卷，令謁前代碑壟，使還，歸職太原。

translations.literal: Jingyi, because his remote ancestor was of Zhao commandery, when he met Rong received his display of hometown respect; Rong sent his aide Li Zhu with three juan of the Zanhuang Collection, ordering him to visit the tombs and steles of former generations. When the envoy returned, Jingyi resumed duty at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyi's distant ancestors came from Zhao; Wang Rong received him with the courtesy due a fellow townsman, sent his aide Li Zhu with three juan of the Zanhuang Collection, and had him visit the family tombs and steles of earlier generations. When the mission ended, Jingyi returned to duty at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 監軍張承業尤不悅本朝宰輔子孫，待敬義甚薄，或面折於公宴，或指言德裕過惡，敬義不得志，鬱憤而卒。

translations.literal: Supervising commander Zhang Chengye especially disliked descendants of this dynasty's chief ministers and treated Jingyi very coldly, sometimes rebuking him to his face at public banquets or pointing out Deyu's faults and crimes; Jingyi could not achieve his aims and died of depressed anger.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch commander Zhang Chengye especially disliked descendants of Tang chief ministers and treated Jingyi harshly, sometimes humiliating him at public feasts or reciting Li Deyu's faults; Jingyi failed to prosper and died of grief and anger.

sentences.zh: 同光二年，贈右僕射。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongguang he was posthumously enfeoffed as Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongguang year two he was posthumously honored as Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: （《五代史闕文》：司空圖，字表聖，自言泗州人。

translations.literal: (Lost Texts of the History of the Five Dynasties: Sikong Tu, style name Biaosheng, said himself to be a man of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: (Lost Texts of the History of the Five Dynasties: Sikong Tu, style name Biaosheng, said he was from Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 少有俊才，威通中，一舉登進士第。

translations.literal: In youth he had outstanding talent; in the Xiantong era he passed the jinshi examination in a single attempt.
translations.idiomatic: He showed outstanding talent in youth and passed the jinshi examination at one sitting in the Xiantong reign.

sentences.zh: 雅好為文，躁於進取，頗臬矜伐，端士鄙之。

translations.literal: He elegantly loved writing, was restless in seeking advancement, rather proud and boastful, and upright gentlemen despised him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved literature, was impatient for advancement, rather vain and boastful, and upright gentlemen despised him for it.

sentences.zh: 初，從事使府，及登朝，驟曆清要。

translations.literal: At first he served in military commissioners' offices; once he entered court he swiftly passed through pure and important posts.
translations.idiomatic: He first served in provincial staffs; once he reached court he rose swiftly through the most coveted offices.

sentences.zh: 巢賊之亂，車駕播遷，圖有先人舊業在中條山，極林泉之美，圖自禮部員外郎，因避地焉，日以詩酒自娛。

translations.literal: In the Huang Chao rebellion the imperial carriage was driven abroad; Tu had his forebears' old estate on Mount Zhongtiao, where forests and springs were supremely beautiful. Tu, from his post as Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites, took refuge there and daily amused himself with poetry and wine.
translations.idiomatic: During Huang Chao's rebellion the court fled; Tu held his family's old estate on Mount Zhongtiao, famed for forest and spring. As Vice Director of Rites he took refuge there and passed his days in poetry and wine.

sentences.zh: 屬天下板蕩，士多往依之，互相推獎，由是聲名藉甚。

translations.literal: As the realm was in turmoil, many scholars went to rely on him and praised one another; because of this his fame spread greatly.
translations.idiomatic: With the realm in turmoil, scholars flocked to him and praised one another, and his fame spread far.

sentences.zh: 昭宗反正，以戶部侍郎征至京師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong restored order, he was summoned to the capital as Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong restored order, Tu was summoned to the capital as Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 圖既負才慢世，謂己當為宰輔，時要惡之，稍抑其銳，圖憤憤謝病，復歸中條。

translations.literal: Tu, relying on his talent and scorning the age, thought he ought to be chief minister; men in power disliked him and slightly checked his edge. Tu indignantly pleaded illness and returned again to Zhongtiao.
translations.idiomatic: Tu, proud of his talent and scornful of the age, believed he should be chief minister; the powerful disliked him and checked his rise. Indignant, he pleaded illness and returned to Mount Zhongtiao.

sentences.zh: 與人書疏，不名官位，但稱知非子，又稱耐辱居士。

translations.literal: In letters to others he did not name his office but only called himself Master Who Knows His Faults, and also Recluse Who Endures Insult.
translations.idiomatic: In correspondence he never used his titles, signing only as Master Who Knows His Faults or Recluse Who Endures Insult.

sentences.zh: 其所居曰禎貽溪，溪上結茅屋，命曰休休亭，常自為記雲。

translations.literal: His dwelling was called Zhenyi Stream; above the stream he built a thatched hut and named it the Rest-Rest Pavilion, often writing his own record of it.
translations.idiomatic: His home lay on Zhenyi Stream; above the water he built a thatched hut called the Rest-Rest Pavilion and often wrote accounts of it himself.

sentences.zh: 臣謹案：圖，河中虞鄉人，少有文彩，未為鄉里所稱。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully notes: Tu was a man of Yuxiang in Hezhong; in youth he had literary color but was not praised in his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject notes: Tu came from Yuxiang in Hezhong; as a youth he showed literary promise but won no praise at home.

sentences.zh: 會王凝自尚書郎出為絳刺史，圖以文謁之，大為凝所賞歎，由是知名。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Ning went out from a Secretariat post to be prefect of Jiang; Tu presented writings to him and was greatly admired and praised by Ning, and from this became known.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Ning left the Secretariat to become prefect of Jiang, Tu presented his writings and won Ning's warm admiration, and from that gained his name.

sentences.zh: 未幾，凝入知制誥，遷中書舍人、知貢舉。

translations.literal: Before long Ning entered to manage edicts, was transferred to Secretariat Drafter and placed in charge of the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Ning entered the edict office, became Secretariat Drafter, and took charge of the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 擢圖上第。

translations.literal: He placed Tu in the top rank.
translations.idiomatic: He placed Tu at the head of the list.

sentences.zh: 頃之，凝出為宣州觀察使，辟圖為從事。

translations.literal: Shortly after, Ning went out as surveillance commissioner of Xuanzhou and recruited Tu as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ning became surveillance commissioner of Xuanzhou and recruited Tu as an aide.

sentences.zh: 既渡江，御史府奏圖監察，下詔追之。

translations.literal: After he crossed the river, the Censorate memorialized Tu as Investigating Censor and an edict was issued to recall him.
translations.idiomatic: After he crossed the Yangzi, the Censorate nominated him as investigating censor and the court issued a recall.

sentences.zh: 圖感知己之恩，不忍輕離幕府，滿百日不赴闕，為台司所劾，遂以本官分司。

translations.literal: Tu, feeling his patron's kindness, could not bear lightly to leave the staff office; a full hundred days he did not attend court and was impeached by the Censorate, and thus served in his original rank as a detached official.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful to his patron, Tu could not bear to leave the staff; he failed to report within the hundred-day limit and was impeached by the Censorate, serving out his term as a detached official.

sentences.zh: 久之，征拜禮部員外郎，俄知制誥，故集中有文曰：戀恩稽命，點係洛師，於今十年，方忝綸閣，此豈躁於進取者耶！

translations.literal: After a long time he was summoned and appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites, and soon managed edicts; hence in his collected works there is a text saying: "Cherishing kindness I delayed my commission, was posted to the Luo capital, and only after ten years did I receive the silk pavilion—how is this one restless in seeking advancement!"
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was summoned as Vice Director of Rites and soon managed edicts; his collected works include the line, "Cherishing kindness I delayed my commission, was posted to Luoyang, and only after ten years reached the edict office—was that the conduct of a man restless for office?"

sentences.zh: 舊史不詳，一至於此。

translations.literal: The old histories are not detailed, yet matters go so far as this.
translations.idiomatic: The old histories omit these details, yet the facts run so far as this.

sentences.zh: 圖見唐政多僻，中官用事，知天下必亂，即棄官歸中條山。

translations.literal: Tu saw that Tang government was much perverse and eunuchs held power; knowing the realm must fall into disorder, he immediately abandoned office and returned to Mount Zhongtiao.
translations.idiomatic: Tu saw Tang government growing corrupt and eunuchs in power; knowing chaos must come, he resigned at once and returned to Mount Zhongtiao.

sentences.zh: 尋以中書舍人征，又拜禮部、戶部侍郎，皆不起。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Secretariat Drafter, and again appointed Vice Minister of Rites and Vice Minister of Revenue—all of which he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned as Secretariat Drafter and offered the vice ministries of Rites and Revenue, but accepted none of them.

sentences.zh: 及昭宗播遷華下，圖以密邇乘輿，即時奔問，復辭還山，故詩曰「多病形容五十三，誰憐借笏趙朝參」，此豈有意於相位耶！

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong was driven abroad below Hua, Tu, because he was near the imperial carriage, at once hurried to inquire after him, then declined and returned to the mountains; hence his poem says, "Sick in many ways, my form at fifty-three—who pities the court attendant borrowing his tablet?"—how could this show intent toward the chief ministership!
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong fled to the region below Mount Hua, Tu, living nearby, hurried to pay his respects, then declined and returned to the hills. His poem runs, "Sick at fifty-three, who pities the court attendant clutching his tablet?"—could that be ambition for the chief ministership!

sentences.zh: 河中節度使王重榮請圖撰碑，得絹數千匹，圖致於虞鄉市心，恣鄉人所取，一日而盡。

translations.literal: Wang Chongrong, military commissioner of Hezhong, asked Tu to compose a stele inscription and received several thousand bolts of silk; Tu placed them in the market center of Yuxiang and let the villagers take as they pleased—all was gone in a day.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongrong of Hezhong asked Tu to write a stele and paid him several thousand bolts of silk; Tu piled them in the Yuxiang market and let the townspeople take what they wished—it was all gone in a day.

sentences.zh: 是時盜賊充斥，獨不入王官穀，河中士人依圖避難，全者甚眾。

translations.literal: At that time bandits filled the land, yet none entered Wangguan Valley; scholars of Hezhong relied on Tu to avoid disaster, and very many were preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits filled the land, yet none entered Wangguan Valley; scholars of Hezhong sheltered with Tu, and a great many were spared.

sentences.zh: 昭宗東遷，又以兵部侍郎召至洛下，為柳璨所阻，一謝而退。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong moved east, he was again summoned as Vice Minister of War to Luoyang, was blocked by Liu Can, thanked him once and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong moved east, Tu was again summoned as Vice Minister of War to Luoyang; Liu Can blocked him, and after a single refusal he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 梁祖受禪，以禮部尚書征，辭以老疾，卒時年八十餘。

translations.literal: When the Liang Founder received the abdication, he was summoned as Minister of Rites; Tu declined on grounds of age and illness and died at more than eighty years.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang Founder took the throne, Tu was summoned as Minister of Rites; he declined on grounds of age and illness and died in his eighties.

sentences.zh: 臣又案：梁室大臣，如敬翔、李振、杜曉、楊涉等，皆唐朝舊族，本當忠義立身，重侯累將，三百餘年，一旦委質朱梁，其甚者讚成弑逆。

translations.literal: Your subject further notes: great ministers of Liang, such as Jing Xiang, Li Zhen, Du Xiao, and Yang She, were all old clans of Tang and ought originally to have stood in loyalty and righteousness; heavy marquisates and successive generals for more than three hundred years—yet in a single day they submitted to Zhu Liang, and the worst praised and completed regicide.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject further notes: Liang ministers such as Jing Xiang, Li Zhen, Du Xiao, and Yang She were old Tang families who should have lived by loyalty; for three hundred years their houses had been enfeoffed and their sons had held command—yet in a day they submitted to Zhu Liang, and the worst praised regicide.

sentences.zh: 惟圖以清直避世，終身不事梁祖，故《梁史》揭圖小瑕以泯大節者，良有以也。）〉

translations.literal: Only Tu, through purity and uprightness, avoided the world and all his life did not serve the Liang Founder; therefore the Liang History's raising small flaws of Tu to obscure his great integrity has its reasons.)]
translations.idiomatic: Only Tu, through purity and integrity, withdrew from the world and never served the Liang Founder; the Liang History's harping on his small faults to obscure his great integrity is understandable.)]

sentences.zh: 盧汝弼，

translations.literal: Lu Rubi,
translations.idiomatic: Lu Rubi,

sentences.zh: （《宣和書譜》：汝弼字子諧，祖綸，唐貞元年有詩名。

translations.literal: (Xuanhe Calligraphy Catalogue: Rubi, style name Zixie; his grandfather Lun had a poetic name in the Zhenyuan era of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: (Xuanhe Calligraphy Catalogue: Rubi, style name Zixie; his grandfather Lun was famed for poetry in the Zhenyuan reign.

sentences.zh: 父簡求，為河東節度使。

translations.literal: His father Jianqiu was military commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jianqiu was military commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 汝弼少力學，不喜為世胄，篤誌科舉，登進士第，文彩秀麗，一時士大夫稱之。）〉

translations.literal: Rubi in youth studied hard, disliked being a hereditary noble, was devoted to the examinations, passed the jinshi degree, and his literary color was elegant and beautiful—men of the gentry of the time praised him.)]
translations.idiomatic: Rubi studied hard in youth, disdained resting on his birth, devoted himself to the examinations, passed the jinshi, and won praise from contemporaries for his elegant prose.)]

sentences.zh: 唐昭宗景福中，擢進士第，曆台省。

translations.literal: In the Jingfu era of Emperor Zhaozong of Tang he passed the jinshi and served in the Censorate and Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Zhaozong's Jingfu reign he passed the jinshi and served in the Censorate and Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 昭宗自秦遷洛，時為祠部郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong moved from Qin to Luo, he was at the time Director in the Bureau of Sacrifices and managed edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong moved the capital from Qin to Luoyang, Rubi was Director in the Bureau of Sacrifices and managed edicts.

sentences.zh: 時梁祖淩弱唐室，殄滅衣冠，懼禍渡河，由上黨歸於晉陽。

translations.literal: At the time the Liang Founder bullied and weakened the Tang house and extinguished the gentry; fearing disaster he crossed the river and from Shangdang returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: As the Liang Founder bullied the Tang court and destroyed the gentry, Rubi feared for his life, crossed the Yellow River, and from Shangdang made his way to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 初，武皇平王行瑜，天子許承製授將吏官秩。

translations.literal: At first, when the Martial Emperor pacified Wang Xingyu, the Son of Heaven permitted him to grant officers and clerks ranks by imperial commission.
translations.idiomatic: When the Martial Emperor pacified Wang Xingyu, the emperor allowed him to commission ranks for his officers by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 是時藩侯倔強者，多偽行墨製，武皇恥而不行，長吏皆表授。

translations.literal: At that time stubborn feudal lords mostly falsely issued written commissions; the Martial Emperor was ashamed and would not do so—all senior officers were appointed by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Stubborn regional lords then forged written commissions at will; the Martial Emperor disdained that practice and appointed all senior officers by formal memorial.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗嗣晉王位，承製置吏，又得汝弼，有若符契，由是除補之命，皆出汝弼之手，既而畿內官吏，考課議擬，奔走盈門，頗以賄賂聞，士論少之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong succeeded to the Prince of Jin's throne, he commissioned officials by imperial order and again obtained Rubi—as if by tally and contract; from this appointments and supplements all came from Rubi's hand. Later, for officials within the capital districts in examination and deliberation, those who hurried to his gate filled it; he was rather known for bribes, and opinion among gentlemen thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong succeeded to the Jin throne, he again gained Rubi, as if by fate; thereafter all appointments passed through Rubi's hands. Soon officials of the capital districts thronged his gate for examination and promotion, and he gained a reputation for taking bribes, which lowered him in gentlemen's eyes.

sentences.zh: 洎帝平定趙、魏，汝弼每請謁迎勞，必陳說天命，顒俟中興，帝亦以宰輔期之。

translations.literal: By the time the emperor pacified Zhao and Wei, whenever Rubi requested audience to welcome and comfort him he always expounded the Mandate of Heaven and looked earnestly for restoration; the emperor also expected him for chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor pacified Zhao and Wei, Rubi always sought audience to welcome him and expounded the Mandate of Heaven, looking earnestly for restoration; the emperor likewise expected to make him chief minister.

sentences.zh: 建國前，卒於晉。

translations.literal: Before the founding of the state he died at Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Jinyang before the founding of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: （《宣和書譜》：贈兵部尚書。）〉

translations.literal: (Xuanhe Calligraphy Catalogue: posthumously enfeoffed Minister of War.)]
translations.idiomatic: (Xuanhe Calligraphy Catalogue: posthumously honored as Minister of War.)]

sentences.zh: 李德休，字表逸，趙郡讚皇人也。

translations.literal: Li Dexiu, style name Biaoyi, was a man of Zanhuang in Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dexiu, whose style name was Biaoyi, came from Zanhuang in Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖絳，山南西道節度使，唐史有傳。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jiang was military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit; the Tang histories have his biography.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jiang was military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit and has a biography in the Tang histories.

sentences.zh: 父璋，宣州觀察使。

translations.literal: His father Zhang was surveillance commissioner of Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang was surveillance commissioner of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 德休登進士第，曆鹽鐵官、渭南尉、右補闕、侍御史。

translations.literal: Dexiu passed the jinshi examination and served as salt-and-iron officer, magistrate of Weinan, Right Supplementation Censor, and Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Dexiu passed the jinshi and served as salt-and-iron officer, magistrate of Weinan, Right Supplementation Censor, and attending censor.

sentences.zh: 天祐初，兩京喪亂，乃寓跡河朔，定州節度使王處直辟為從事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianyou, with disorder in the two capitals, he sojourned in Hebei; Wang Chuzhi, military commissioner of Dingzhou, recruited him as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianyou, with both capitals in chaos, he took refuge in Hebei; Wang Chuzhi of Dingzhou recruited him as an aide.

sentences.zh: 莊宗即位於魏州，征為御史中丞，轉兵部、吏部侍郎，權知左丞，以禮部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong took the throne at Weizhou, he was summoned as Censor-in-Chief, transferred to Vice Minister of War and Vice Minister of Personnel, acted as Left Vice Director, and retired as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong took the throne at Weizhou, Dexiu was summoned as censor-in-chief, became vice ministers of War and Personnel, acted as Left Vice Director, and retired as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 卒時年七十四。

translations.literal: When he died he was seventy-four years old.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 蘇循，父特，陳州刺史。

translations.literal: Su Xun—his father Te was prefect of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Su Xun's father Te was prefect of Chen.

sentences.zh: 循，咸通中登進士第，累曆台閣。

translations.literal: Xun passed the jinshi in the Xiantong era and repeatedly served in the Censorate and Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xun passed the jinshi in the Xiantong reign and rose through the Censorate and Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 昭宗朝，再至禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Zhaozong he twice reached the post of Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhaozong he twice served as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 循性阿諛，善承順苟容，以希進取。

translations.literal: Xun's nature was fawning and flattering; he was skilled at complying and accommodating to seek advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was fawning by nature, skilled at compliance and accommodation, and eager for advancement.

sentences.zh: 昭宗自遷洛之後，梁祖凶勢日滋，唐室舊臣，陰懷主辱之憤，名族之胄，往往有違禍不仕者，唯循希旨附會。

translations.literal: After Emperor Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, the Liang Founder's fierce power grew daily; old ministers of the Tang house secretly harbored anger at their lord's disgrace, and scions of famous clans often defied disaster and refused office—only Xun pleased intent and attached himself.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, the Liang Founder's power grew daily; old Tang ministers nursed secret shame for their sovereign's humiliation, and sons of great families often refused office to avoid disaster—only Xun flattered every whim.

sentences.zh: 及梁祖失律於淮南，西屯於壽春，要少帝欲授九錫。

translations.literal: When the Liang Founder lost discipline in Huainan and encamped west at Shouchun, he wished the young emperor to grant the Nine Bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang Founder suffered setbacks in Huainan and encamped at Shouchun, he pressed the young emperor to grant him the Nine Bestowals.

sentences.zh: 朝臣或議是非，循揚言云：「梁王功業顯大，曆數有歸，朝廷速宜揖讓。

translations.literal: Some court ministers debated right and wrong; Xun proclaimed aloud: "Prince Liang's achievements and enterprise are manifest and great; the mandate has its return—the court should quickly yield by bowing."
translations.idiomatic: When some courtiers debated the matter, Xun proclaimed aloud, "Prince Liang's achievements are manifest; the mandate has turned to him—the court should yield the throne at once."

sentences.zh: 」當時朝士畏梁祖如虎，罔敢違其言者。

translations.literal: At the time court gentlemen feared the Liang Founder like a tiger and none dared oppose his words.
translations.idiomatic: Court gentlemen then feared the Liang Founder like a tiger, and none dared contradict him.

sentences.zh: 明年，梁祖逼禪，循為冊禮副使。

translations.literal: The next year the Liang Founder forced the abdication; Xun was deputy envoy for the enfeoffment rites.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Liang Founder forced abdication; Xun served as deputy envoy for the enthronement rites.

sentences.zh: 梁祖既受命，宴於元德殿，舉酒曰：「朕夾輔日淺，代德未隆，置朕及此者，群公推崇之意也。

translations.literal: Once the Liang Founder had received the Mandate, he feasted in the Hall of Primary Virtue and raised his cup, saying: "My days aiding the throne have been short, and the virtue of my house is not yet lofty; that I have been placed here is the intent of you lords in promoting me."
translations.idiomatic: After receiving the Mandate, the Liang Founder feasted in the Hall of Primary Virtue and raised his cup: "I have aided the throne but briefly, and my house's virtue is not yet lofty; I stand here through your lords' promotion."

sentences.zh: 」楊涉、張文蔚慚懼失對，致謝而已。

translations.literal: Yang She and Zhang Wenwei, ashamed and afraid, lost their replies and only offered thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Yang She and Zhang Wenwei, ashamed and afraid, could find no reply and only thanked him.

sentences.zh: 循與張禕、薛貽矩因盛陳梁祖之德業，應天順人之美。

translations.literal: Xun with Zhang Yi and Xue Yiju thereupon lavishly set forth the Liang Founder's virtue and enterprise and the beauty of responding to Heaven and following men.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, Zhang Yi, and Xue Yiju thereupon lavishly praised the Liang Founder's virtue and the beauty of his accord with Heaven and the people.

sentences.zh: 循自以奉冊之勞，旦夕望居宰輔，而敬翔惡其為人，謂梁祖曰：「聖祚維新，宜選端士，以鎮風俗。

translations.literal: Xun, considering his labor in presenting the enfeoffment documents, morning and evening looked to occupy the chief ministry; but Jing Xiang detested his character and said to the Liang Founder: "The sacred reign is newly renewed—it is fitting to select upright gentlemen to steady custom and teaching."
translations.idiomatic: Xun, counting on his service in the enthronement rites, expected soon to become chief minister; but Jing Xiang detested him and told the Liang Founder, "The sacred reign is newly renewed—you should choose upright men to steady the manners of the age."

sentences.zh: 如循等輩，俱無士行，實唐家之鴟梟，當今之狐魅，彼專賣國以取利，不可立維新之朝。」

translations.literal: Men like Xun and his kind all lack the conduct of gentlemen; they are in truth Tang's owl and bat, the fox-spirits of the present age—those who specialize in selling the state for profit cannot establish a renewed court."
translations.idiomatic: Men like Xun lack the conduct of gentlemen; they are Tang's owls and bats, the fox-spirits of our age—men who sell the state for profit cannot build a renewed court."

sentences.zh: 初，循子楷，乾寧二年登進士第。

translations.literal: At first Xun's son Kai passed the jinshi in the second year of Qianning.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's son Kai passed the jinshi in the second year of Qianning.

sentences.zh: 中使有奏禦者云：「今年進士二十餘人，僥幸者半，物論以為不可。

translations.literal: An inner envoy memorialized to the emperor: "This year there are more than twenty jinshi graduates, and half are lucky strikers—public opinion holds this unacceptable."
translations.idiomatic: An imperial eunuch reported to the throne, "This year's jinshi number more than twenty, and half won their degrees by luck—public opinion calls that unacceptable."

sentences.zh: 」昭宗命學士陸扆、馮渥重試於雲韶殿，及格者一十四人。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong ordered Academicians Lu Yi and Feng Wo to re-examine them in the Hall of Cloud Music; those who passed were fourteen persons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong ordered Academicians Lu Yi and Feng Wo to re-examine them in the Hall of Cloud Music; only fourteen passed.

sentences.zh: 詔云：「蘇楷、盧賡等四人，詩句最卑，蕪累頗甚，曾無學業，敢竊科名，浼我至公，難從濫進，宜付所司落下，不得再赴舉場。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Su Kai, Lu Geng, and four others—their poetic lines are lowest, their redundancy is excessive, they never had learning yet dared steal examination names, staining my utmost fairness; it is hard to follow indiscriminate advancement. They should be handed to the proper office to be struck from the list and may not again attend the examination grounds."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared, "Su Kai, Lu Geng, and four others wrote the meanest verse, piled redundancy upon redundancy, had no learning yet stole degrees, and stained the court's fairness—they are struck from the rolls and barred from the examination grounds forever."

sentences.zh: 」楷以此慚恨，長幸國家之災。

translations.literal: Kai from this felt shame and resentment and for long rejoiced in the state's disasters.
translations.idiomatic: Kai nursed shame and resentment from this and long rejoiced in the state's misfortunes.

sentences.zh: 昭宗遇弑，輝王嗣位，國命出於朱氏，楷始得為起居郎。
