translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong met assassination, Prince Hui succeeded; the nation's mandate issued from the Zhu clan, and Kai at last became Attendant of the Imperial Diary.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhaozong was murdered and Prince Hui succeeded, with the Zhu clan holding the mandate, Kai at last became Attendant of the Imperial Diary.

sentences.zh: 柳璨陷害朝臣，衣冠惕息，無敢言者。

translations.literal: Liu Can framed court ministers; gentry in official dress trembled and held their breath, and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can framed court ministers; the gentry trembled in silence, and none dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 初，梁祖欲以張廷範為太常卿，裴樞以為不可。

translations.literal: At first the Liang Founder wished to make Zhang Tingfan Minister of Ceremonies; Pei Shu held it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Liang Founder wished to name Zhang Tingfan Minister of Ceremonies; Pei Shu opposed it.

sentences.zh: 柳璨懼梁祖之毒，乃歸過於樞，故裴、趙罹白馬之禍。

translations.literal: Liu Can feared the Liang Founder's venom and shifted blame onto Shu; therefore Pei and Zhao suffered the disaster at Baima.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can, fearing the Founder's wrath, shifted blame onto Shu; thus Pei and Zhao suffered the massacre at Baima.

sentences.zh: 楷因附璨，復依廷範。

translations.literal: Kai therefore attached himself to Can and again relied on Tingfan.
translations.idiomatic: Kai attached himself to Can and again relied on Tingfan.

sentences.zh: 時有司初定昭宗諡號，楷謂廷範曰：「諡者所以表行實，前有司之諡先帝為昭宗，所謂名實不副。

translations.literal: At the time the proper offices first fixed Emperor Zhaozong's posthumous title; Kai said to Tingfan: "A posthumous name is meant to display conduct in fact; the former offices' posthumous name for the late emperor as Zhaozong is what is called name and reality not matching."
translations.idiomatic: When the proper offices first fixed Zhaozong's posthumous title, Kai told Tingfan, "A posthumous name should reflect true conduct; to call the late emperor Zhaozong is a mismatch of name and reality."

sentences.zh: 司空為樂卿，餘忝史職，典章有失，安得不言。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works is master of music; I am unworthy in the historian's office—when statutes and regulations err, how can I not speak?
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Works oversees music; I hold a historian's post—when ritual law errs, how can I remain silent?

sentences.zh: 」乃上疏曰：「帝王禦宇，察理亂以審汙隆；

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial saying: "Emperors and kings govern the realm, examining order and disorder to judge rise and fall;
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized: "Emperors govern the realm by discerning order from chaos and rise from fall;

sentences.zh: 祀享配天，資諡號以定升降。

translations.literal: in sacrifice and offering they match Heaven, relying on posthumous names to fix ascent and descent.
translations.idiomatic: in sacrifice they match Heaven, relying on posthumous names to fix honor high or low.

sentences.zh: 故臣下君上，皆不得而私也。

translations.literal: Therefore subject and sovereign alike may not treat this as private.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore neither subject nor sovereign may treat this as a private matter.

sentences.zh: 先帝睿哲居尊，恭儉垂化，其於善美，孰敢蔽虧。

translations.literal: The late emperor, wise and sagacious in his seat, spread respectful frugality as transformation—who would dare conceal or diminish his goodness and beauty?
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor was wise upon the throne and spread respectful frugality—who would dare conceal his virtues?

sentences.zh: 然而否運莫興，至理猶鬱，遂致四方多事，萬乘播遷。

translations.literal: Yet adverse fortune did not rise, supreme principle still was depressed, and thus the four quarters had many affairs and the imperial carriage was driven abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Yet fortune did not turn, supreme principle remained blocked, the four quarters erupted in trouble, and the imperial carriage was driven into exile.

sentences.zh: 始則宦豎凶狂，受幽辱於東內；

translations.literal: at first eunuch attendants were fierce and mad, and he suffered seclusion and insult in the Eastern Inner Palace;
translations.idiomatic: First eunuch attendants ran wild and he suffered insult in the Eastern Inner Palace;

sentences.zh: 終則嬪嬙悖亂，罹夭閼於中闈。

translations.literal: in the end consorts and concubines were rebellious and disorderly, and he met untimely obstruction in the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: in the end consorts rebelled and he met untimely death within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 其於易名，宜循考行。

translations.literal: In changing his name, one should follow and examine his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In choosing a new name, one should follow and examine his conduct.

sentences.zh: 有司先定尊諡曰聖穆景文孝皇帝，廟號昭宗，敢言溢美，似異直書。

translations.literal: The proper offices first fixed the honored posthumous title as Sagacious, Solemn, Illustrious, Cultured, Filial Emperor, with temple name Zhaozong—I dare say it overflows with praise and seems unlike straightforward writing.
translations.idiomatic: The proper offices first fixed his posthumous title as Sagacious, Solemn, Illustrious, Cultured, Filial Emperor and his temple name as Zhaozong—a title so lavish it seems unlike honest record.

sentences.zh: 今郊禋有日，祫祭惟時，將期允愜列聖之心，更在詳議新廟之稱，庶使葉先朝罪己之德，表聖上無私之明。」

translations.literal: Now the suburban sacrifice has its day and the collective ancestral rite has its season; we will look to satisfy the hearts of the ranked sages, and further deliberate in detail the new temple designation, hoping thereby to accord with the late dynasty's virtue of blaming itself and display the present sage's impartial clarity."
translations.idiomatic: The suburban sacrifice draws near and the collective ancestral rite is due; we must satisfy the former sages and deliberate anew the temple designation, that we may honor the late dynasty's virtue of self-reproach and display the present sovereign's impartial clarity."

sentences.zh: （《舊唐書》云：蘇楷目不知書，僅能執筆，其文羅袞作也。）〉

translations.literal: (Old Book of Tang says: Su Kai's eyes did not know books; he could barely hold the brush—his texts were written by Luo Gun.)]
translations.idiomatic: (Old Book of Tang: Su Kai could scarcely read; he could barely hold a brush—his essays were written by Luo Gun.)]

sentences.zh: 太常卿張廷範奏議曰：「昭宗初實彰於聖德，後漸減於休明，致季述幽辱於前，茂貞劫幸於後，雖數拘厄運，亦道失始終。

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Tingfan submitted a deliberation saying: "Emperor Zhaozong at first truly displayed sagely virtue, but later gradually diminished in glorious clarity, bringing Ji's seclusion and insult in front and Maozhen's seizing the imperial progress behind—though he several times met obstructed fortune, he also lost the Way in beginning and end."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Tingfan submitted: "Zhaozong at first showed true sagely virtue, but later his glory faded; Ji kept him captive and Maozhen seized the court—though ill fortune pressed him repeatedly, he also lost the Way from first to last."

sentences.zh: 違陵寢於西京，徙兆民於東洛，軔輦輅未逾於寒暑，行大事俄起於宮闈。

translations.literal: He departed from the imperial tombs in the Western Capital, moved the myriad people to Eastern Luo; the imperial carriage had not passed a season of cold and heat before great affairs suddenly arose in the palace women's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned the tombs in Chang'an, moved the people to Luoyang; scarcely a season passed before catastrophe struck within the palace.

sentences.zh: 謹聞執事堅固之謂恭，亂而不損之謂靈，武而不遂之謂莊，在國逢難之謂閔，因事有功之謂襄。

translations.literal: I have respectfully heard that firm solidity is called Gong, disorder without harm is called Ling, martial effort without completion is called Zhuang, meeting hardship in the state is called Min, and achievement through events is called Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that firmness is called Gong, surviving disorder unharmed is Ling, martial effort uncompleted is Zhuang, meeting national hardship is Min, and merit through events is Xiang.

sentences.zh: 今請改諡曰恭靈莊閔皇帝，廟號襄宗。

translations.literal: Now I request changing the posthumous title to Respectful, Spirited, Solemn, Sorrowful Emperor, with temple name Emperor Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: I request the posthumous title Respectful, Spirited, Solemn, Sorrowful Emperor and the temple name Emperor Xiang.

sentences.zh: 」輝王答詔曰：「勉依所奏，哀咽良深。

translations.literal: Prince Hui replied by edict: "I reluctantly follow what was submitted; my grief chokes deep."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hui replied, "I reluctantly follow your submission; my grief is profound."

sentences.zh: 」楷附會幸災也如是。

translations.literal: Thus did Kai attach himself to others' words and rejoice in disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Such was Kai's way of attaching himself to power and rejoicing in disaster.

sentences.zh: 及梁祖即位於汴，楷自以遭遇千載一時，敬翔深鄙其行。

translations.literal: When the Liang Founder took the throne at Bian, Kai considered himself to have met a once-in-a-thousand-years moment; Jing Xiang deeply despised his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang Founder took the throne at Bian, Kai thought he had met a once-in-a-millennium chance; Jing Xiang despised his conduct.

sentences.zh: 尋有詔云：「蘇楷、高貽休、蕭聞禮等，人才寢陋，不可塵穢班行，並勒歸田里。

translations.literal: Soon an edict said: "Su Kai, Gao Yixiu, Xiao Wenli, and others—their talent grows ever more base and cannot defile the court ranks; all are ordered to return to their fields."
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict declared, "Su Kai, Gao Yixiu, Xiao Wenli, and others are base in talent and must not stain the court ranks—all are ordered home to their fields."

sentences.zh: 」循、楷既失所望，懼以前過獲罪，乃退歸河中依朱友謙。

translations.literal: Xun and Kai, having lost what they hoped for, feared punishment for former faults and therefore withdrew to Hezhong to rely on Zhu Youqian.
translations.idiomatic: Xun and Kai, disappointed in their hopes, feared punishment for past faults and withdrew to Hezhong to serve Zhu Youqian.

sentences.zh: 莊宗將即位於魏州，時百官多缺，乃求訪本朝衣冠，友謙令赴行台。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong was about to take the throne at Weizhou, many offices among the hundred officials were vacant; he sought out gentry in official dress of this dynasty, and Youqian ordered them to go to the mobile headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhuangzong prepared to take the throne at Weizhou, many offices stood empty; he sought men of the old Tang gentry, and Youqian sent Xun to the mobile headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時張承業未欲莊宗即尊位，諸將賓僚無敢讚成者，及循至，入衙城見府廨即拜，謂之拜殿。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Chengye did not yet wish Zhuangzong to assume the exalted throne; among generals and guest officials none dared praise and approve. When Xun arrived, he entered the yamen city, saw the commandery offices and at once bowed—this was called bowing to the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chengye did not yet wish Zhuangzong to assume the throne; none of the generals or staff dared approve. When Xun arrived he entered the headquarters, saw the offices, and bowed at once—this was called bowing to the hall.

sentences.zh: 時將吏未行蹈舞禮，及循朝謁，即呼萬歲舞抃，泣而稱臣，莊宗大悅。

translations.literal: At the time officers had not yet performed the treading-and-dancing rite; when Xun attended audience he at once cried "Ten thousand years," danced with clapping, wept and called himself subject—Emperor Zhuangzong was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The officers had not yet performed the court dance; at audience Xun cried "Long live the emperor," danced and clapped, wept, and declared himself a subject—Zhuangzong was delighted.

sentences.zh: 翌日，又獻大筆三十管，曰「畫日筆」，莊宗益喜。

translations.literal: The next day he again presented thirty large brushes, calling them "sun-painting brushes," and Emperor Zhuangzong was still more pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he presented thirty large brushes called "sun-painting brushes," and Zhuangzong was still more pleased.

sentences.zh: 承業聞之怒，會盧汝弼卒，即令循守本官，代為副使。

translations.literal: Chengye heard of it and was angry; it happened that Lu Rubi died, and he at once had Xun keep his original office and replace him as deputy envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye heard and was furious; when Lu Rubi died, he had Xun keep his old post and replace him as deputy envoy.

sentences.zh: 明年春，循因食蜜雪，傷寒而卒。

translations.literal: In the spring of the next year Xun, from eating honeyed snow, contracted cold damage and died.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring Xun ate chilled honeyed snow, took cold, and died.

sentences.zh: 同光二年，贈左僕射，以楷為員外郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongguang he was posthumously enfeoffed Left Vice Director, and Kai was made Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongguang year two he was posthumously honored as Left Vice Director, and Kai was named Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 天成中，累曆使幕，會執政欲糾其駁諡之罪，竟以憂慚而卒。

translations.literal: In the Tiancheng era he repeatedly served in commissioners' staffs; it happened that those in power wished to prosecute his crime of rejecting the posthumous title, and in the end he died of worry and shame.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tiancheng he served repeatedly in commissioners' staffs; when the authorities moved to prosecute him for rejecting Zhaozong's posthumous title, he died of shame and grief.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：昔武皇之樹霸基，莊宗之開帝業，皆旁求多士，用佐丕圖。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: In the past, when the Martial Emperor planted the foundation of hegemony and Emperor Zhuangzong opened the imperial enterprise, both broadly sought many scholars to assist their great designs.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: When the Martial Emperor laid the foundations of hegemony and Zhuangzong opened the imperial enterprise, both sought scholars broadly to assist their great designs.

sentences.zh: 故數君子者，或以書檄敏才，或以搢紳舊族，鹹登貴仕，諒亦宜哉！

translations.literal: Therefore these several gentlemen, whether by nimble talent in letters and proclamations or by gentry of old clans, all ascended to exalted office—surely this was fitting!
translations.idiomatic: These gentlemen, whether by nimble pen in letters and proclamations or by birth in old gentry families, all rose to high office—and rightly so!

sentences.zh: 唯蘇循讚梁祖之強禪，蘇楷駁昭宗之舊諡，士風臣節，豈若是乎！

translations.literal: Only Su Xun praised the Liang Founder's forced abdication and Su Kai rejected Emperor Zhaozong's old posthumous title—can scholar custom and ministerial integrity be like this!
translations.idiomatic: Only Su Xun praised the Liang Founder's forced abdication and Su Kai rejected Zhaozong's posthumous title—can scholarly integrity and ministerial duty sink so low!

sentences.zh: 斯蓋文苑之豺狼，儒林之荊棘也。

translations.literal: These are jackals and wolves of the literary grove, thorns and brambles of the Confucian forest.
translations.idiomatic: They are jackals and wolves in the grove of letters, thorns in the forest of scholars.
